c.v: This stage proves that a recorded run can stand in for a live one. We gave the monitor a parameter that writes down every heartbeat it receives, with the time on its own clock, then recorded a live run with
and played the same bag into a fresh monitor to compare what each one actually heard.

The decision worth defending is what "the same inputs" means. Each run can miss a few heartbeats at its start while discovery finishes, so a plain difference between the two files would report a mismatch that says nothing about the replay. The comparison instead starts at the later of the two first values it saw and ends at the earlier of the two last ones, and only inside that shared stretch does every heartbeat have to match.
What we can now show: our comparison tool prints
and exits 0 for a live run and its replay, at normal speed and at double speed, with or without simulation time. What it also shows is that only a monitor replayed on the recording's own clock, with
, reproduces the live timing, which is exactly what anything that judges by elapsed time, such as the bench's own supervisor, will depend on.

subs.title: Record a run and replay it into the bench

c.v: By the end of this session, the monitor writes down every heartbeat it receives, a run of the bench is recorded in a bag, and the same bag played into a fresh monitor gives it the heartbeats the live monitor got.

The bench's scenarios will fail now and then, and a failure you can't bring back is hard to fix. A bag keeps what the nodes received, so you can play it into the node under suspicion as often as you like, without the simulator. That only helps if the replay really gives the node the same inputs, so this topic measures it, on the simplest node the bench has. The inspection topic showed the commands on turtlesim; here they run on your own nodes.

That difference is the reason this topic exists. The monitor only counts, so its verdicts don't depend on time. The supervisor in the next topic decides by the age of the last odometry message and of the last command on its own clock, and a replay reproduces those decisions only when its clock follows the recording.
